inputs.share_count_basis: 2,676.34m ordinary shares in issue at 30 Jun 2026 (H1 FY2026 interim; unchanged since the Sep-2025 IPO). Basic = diluted per the interim EPS note (no dilutive options; awarded-share scheme immaterial). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows (~0.03% of revenue) and there is no announced non-SBC issuance. Parent Zijin Mining Group holds ~85%.
inputs.sbc_source: Statement of changes in equity / cash-flow add-back: FY2025 US$1.424m, H1 FY2026 US$1.135m, H1 FY2025 US$0.298m -> TTM Jun-2026 US$2.26m. Equity-award taxes nil (EquityAwardTaxes kpi = 0). SBC-zero market in practice; rows kept explicit.
inputs.fx_note: Statements are in USD (read off the FY2025 annual and H1 FY2026 interim); the HKEX quote is HKD. USD->HKD 7.8479 from Yahoo HKD=X, 2026-10-17 (weak edge of the 7.75-7.85 HKMA peg band, so the rate is effectively fixed). No dual listing to parity-check against; the peg is the check. Engine values computed in USD and converted at this rate; unsuffixed per-share values are HKD.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-16T08:08:14Z HKEX regular close (Yahoo regularMarketTime; Fri close, market shut for weekend)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, so a USD-built rate: 10y UST ~4.3% + beta ~0.95 x 5.0% ERP = ~9.0%, plus ~0.5pp for a portfolio that is overwhelmingly in emerging/frontier jurisdictions (Colombia, Suriname, Guyana, Ghana, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Kazakhstan, PNG JV) = 9.5%. Same rate in every scenario (risk charged once): gold-price risk lives in the scenario flows, not in a WACC premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease liabilities US$80.6m (27.3 current + 53.3 non-current) are in total_debt; lease principal (~US$32m/yr) is NOT deducted from flows; lease_cost_pct_path = 0. Immaterial either way.
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the flows: NCI took 14.5% of FY2025 and 12.5% of H1 FY2026 profit (Buritica, Rosebel, Jilau/Taror, Taldybulak are not 100%-owned). Folded into cash_tax_rate_path as a combined tax+NCI leakage: 1 - (1 - 31% cash tax) x (1 - 13% NCI) = ~40%. Calibration: TTM underlying EBIT US$4,032m x (1 - 40.5%) = US$2,399m vs reported TTM attributable profit US$2,532m less Porgera JV share (~US$158m) and after-tax net interest (~US$26m) = ~US$2,348m, a 2% tie. NCI book (US$564m) is therefore NOT deducted in the bridge.
inputs.notes:
MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component build) with the non-US/cyclical adaptations, on a mid-cycle gold-price deck. Routing: a producing gold miner is an operating company whose value is a free-cash-flow stream, so owner-FCF is the right family; but it is a commodity price-taker (97.8% of revenue gold-linked, no hedging), so the revenue line is built from VOLUME x a normalized GOLD PRICE deck rather than extrapolated from FY2025 / H1 FY2026, which sat on a US$3,524 and US$4,643/oz realised price respectively. No prior DCF and no MEMORY.md entry: first valuation.

FY0 = TTM to 30 Jun 2026 (FY2025 + H1 FY2026 - H1 FY2025), chosen over FY2025 because the valuation date is four months after the interim balance sheet and FY2025 includes only part-year Akyem (Apr-25) and Raygorodok (Oct-25). TTM revenue US$7,373m; TTM gold sales 1.705Moz (1.498 + 0.840 - 0.633); revenue per oz sold US$4,324 vs ~US$4,232 realised gold = ~2% by-product uplift.

REVENUE = 1.02 x gold price x consolidated ounces sold. Volumes: 2026 guidance 59.2t includes Porgera 3.3t attributable (equity-accounted, not in revenue) -> 55.9t consolidated (~1.80Moz); 2028 guidance 70-75t incl. Porgera -> ~67-72t consolidated as the five expansions (Raygorodok, Akyem, Rosebel plant, Saramacca, Jilau/Taror) commission Q1-Q3 2028. Base path (Moz, Jun-years): 1.82, 1.93, 2.13, 2.25, 2.28, 2.28 then a gentle depletion decline to 2.15 by Y10 (917t reserves = ~13yr at 70t). Gold deck (US$/oz realised; spot GC=F ~4,181 on 2026-10-17): base 4,050 / 3,800 / 3,600 then +2%/yr nominal; bull 4,500 / 4,700 / 4,800 then +2.5%; bear 3,700 / 3,100 / 2,800 then +2%.

EBITDA margin = 1 - fixed cash cost per oz / revenue per oz - 8% price-linked costs (royalties scale with price; AISC rose to US$1,678 in H1 FY2026 for that reason). Fixed cost calibrated to H1 FY2026 underlying EBITDA (reported operating profit + D&A, LESS interest income US$86m and Porgera JV share US$88m, which are both carried in the bridge instead): US$1,602/oz all-in cash cost at US$4,746/oz revenue -> ~US$1,220/oz fixed; held roughly flat in nominal terms Y3-Y5 as the expansions bring scale, then +2.5%/yr. TTM underlying EBITDA margin was 65.7% (excludes the US$78m Bullabulling disposal gain in H1 FY2025). D&A ~US$490/oz rising to ~US$560/oz as the US$3.2bn of growth capex depreciates. Capex: sustaining ~US$340/oz +2.5%/yr, plus growth capex US$1,250m / 1,250m / 400m in Y1-Y3 (announced project budgets sum to ~US$3.17bn: Raygorodok 910, Akyem 690, Rosebel 700, Saramacca 570, HFO power 200, Jilau/Taror 100; bear assumes ~15% overrun), then ~US$600/oz (+2.5%/yr) all-in from Y4 including reserve replacement, ~1.1x D&A, so the terminal year funds its own depletion. Working capital -8% of the revenue change (inventory 711 + receivables 302 - payables 408 = ~7.6% of run-rate revenue; growth consumes cash).

OWNER FCF (TTM): reported FCF 3,044.5 (OCF 3,783.4 - PPE+intangibles capex 738.9) - SBC 2.3 - interest income 124.6 (net cash 3.4bn >> 1x FCF base, so stripped) = 2,917.6. Projected year-1 owner FCF is far lower (~US$1.3bn) because growth capex roughly triples and the deck steps down from the TTM average price; that gap is deliberate, not a carried-forward one-off.

BRIDGE: cash US$3,869m less borrowings US$430.0m (343.3 current + 86.7 non-current) and leases US$80.6m at 30 Jun 2026; restricted cash US$106m excluded. equity_bridge carries post-balance-sheet and non-operating items (see that block). Buybacks nil: the flat share count is a modelling convention, not something the company funds (it pays dividends instead - HK$1.50 interim, first since listing).

M&A: the Jan-2026 proposal to acquire all of Allied Gold for ~US$4.0bn did not complete as a takeover; on 29 Jul 2026 the company instead subscribed for a 9.2% stake (US$295m, completed 10 Aug 2026). Further acquisitions are NOT modelled - deals at fair value are value-neutral, and the parent's acquisition record is a bull-case argument, not a base-case cash flow.

SBC-zero market: house and street coincide, band_position should be read as n/a (collapsed band).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case revenue CAGR TTM Jun-2026 -> Y5 (volume +5.4%/yr offset by the gold deck stepping down from the TTM average realised price). Used because every historical CAGR here is distorted: FY2022-25 revenue rides a 75% gold-price rise plus acquisitions, equity is inflated by US$6.7bn of IPO/placement proceeds, EPS is not comparable across the pre-IPO reorganised share count, and owner FCF has only two clean annual points.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 66.8% vs revenue 43.6% (>30% divergence): equity jump is the Sep-2025 IPO capital (US$6.73bn share proceeds) less the US$2.1bn reorganisation payment to Zijin Mining Group, not retained earnings. Not a usable growth signal.
historical_growth.notes: FY2022-FY2025 history is pre-IPO carve-out accounts (5 years not available). Owner-FCF growth FY2024->TTM (379 -> 2,918) is almost entirely gold price (realised ~US$2,390 -> ~4,232/oz) plus the Akyem and Raygorodok acquisitions; SBC is immaterial so owner and reported FCF CAGRs do not diverge. Guided mined production CAGR 2025->2028 is ~15.6%/yr (46.9t -> 70-75t incl. Porgera) - that is the volume growth the base case captures.

base.cash_tax_rate_note: Combined ~31% cash tax (blend of Colombia/Suriname/Ghana ~35%, Australia 30%, Guyana 25%, Kazakhstan 20%, Kyrgyz/Tajik lower, plus dividend withholding on upstreaming; FY2025 book ETR 32%, H1 FY2026 30%) and ~13% NCI leakage.
base.narrative: Gold mean-reverts from spot (~US$4,180) to a US$3,600 mid-cycle by Y3 and then tracks inflation; volume follows guidance with a modest haircut (2028 consolidated ~70t, at the low end of 70-75t incl. Porgera) and then depletes slowly. Margins settle near 59% vs 66% TTM.

bull.cash_tax_rate_note: Higher than base: at US$4,800+ gold, windfall/royalty tightening by host states (the Porgera precedent) is more likely, not less.
bull.narrative: Structural regime shift holds: central-bank and ETF demand keep gold at US$4,500-4,800 and rising 2.5%/yr; expansions deliver the top of 2028 guidance and Akyem reaches ~13t, taking consolidated output to ~76t.

bear.narrative: Gold reverts to US$2,800 by Y3 (still ~17% above the 2024 average) as real rates rise and official-sector buying fades; expansions slip and overrun ~15%; consolidated output peaks ~65t and depletes faster. Terminal growth 1% reflects a shorter reserve life.

scenario_narratives.base: Zijin Gold is a mid-tier, fast-growing, unhedged gold producer, so the only questions are the gold price, the volume ramp and how much host governments and minorities take. Base: gold eases from ~US$4,180 spot to a US$3,600 mid-cycle by mid-2029 and then rises with inflation; the five expansions (US$3.2bn, commissioning Q1-Q3 2028) lift consolidated output from ~1.80Moz in 2026 to ~2.25-2.28Moz, then reserves deplete slowly. Royalties scale with price, so EBITDA margin settles near 59% (66% TTM). Growth capex roughly triples spending for two years, depressing Y1-Y2 owner FCF to ~US$1.1-1.3bn before it recovers to ~US$2.2bn. No M&A is modelled.
scenario_narratives.bull: The regime shift the company describes (official-sector reserve diversification, fiscal and geopolitical fragmentation) holds: gold stays US$4,500-4,800 and compounds 2.5%/yr, the expansions hit the top of the 70-75t 2028 guidance and Akyem's 13.5Mtpa expansion takes it to ~13t, margins widen to ~68%. Partly offset by a heavier host-state take (42% combined leakage). Parent-backed M&A could add more, but is not counted because deals at fair value do not create value for the buyer.
scenario_narratives.bear: Gold reverts to US$2,800 as real rates rise and central-bank buying fades, the kind of 30-40% drawdown that followed the 1980 and 2011 peaks; expansions slip and overrun ~15% in emerging-market jurisdictions (Kazakhstan, Ghana, Suriname); output peaks ~65t; margins compress to ~50% as fixed costs and royalties bite. The balance sheet (US$3.4bn net cash) means this is a value case, not a solvency case. Resource-nationalism events (a Porgera-style licence loss at one mine) are a further tail inside this scenario's weight rather than modelled separately.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 30%: the earnings base sits on a gold price at an all-time real high, and every prior gold super-cycle (1980, 2011) was followed by a 40%+ drawdown; the jurisdiction mix adds licence/tax risk. Base 50%: a mid-cycle reversion to ~US$3,600 is the central expectation. Bull cut to 20%: it needs gold to hold near record levels for a decade AND flawless execution of five simultaneous expansions.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value a price-taking miner on a normalized commodity deck, not on the latest year. FY2025 and H1 FY2026 earnings sit on the highest realised gold prices in history and on a freshly-IPO'd balance sheet; extrapolating them would capitalize the peak. Volumes are taken from management guidance (with a haircut), the gold price from an explicit deck per scenario, costs from H1 FY2026 unit economics with royalties scaling with price, and NCI/tax charged once through a calibrated combined leakage rate. Terminal value capped at 12x owner FCF because the asset base depletes.
key_risks_to_valuation: Gold price: every US$100/oz on the long-run deck is worth roughly US$140m/yr of EBITDA after royalties at ~2.25Moz; the valuation is dominated by this one input
Execution of five concurrent expansions (US$3.2bn, Q1-Q3 2028) in Ghana, Kazakhstan, Suriname and Tajikistan: overruns or slippage hit both capex and the volume ramp
Resource nationalism / fiscal take: Porgera precedent (licence not renewed 2019-20), Ghana and Kazakhstan royalty regimes, windfall taxes are more likely at high prices
Controlled company: Zijin Mining Group ~85%, connected-party sales and services, thin free float; capital allocation (M&A such as the Allied Gold approach) may serve the parent's strategy
Cash tax: H1 FY2026 cash tax paid was 31.5% of PBT vs 17% in FY2025; a structurally higher combined leakage than the 40.5% modelled would cut value further
Model is a single-currency USD build; HKD peg removes FX translation risk for the quote but not operating-currency (AUD, KZT, GHS) cost exposure
